title: Release cutover checklist - 2026-03-14 (scratchpad)
content:
Context: dry-run was yesterday morning, small regression in KV cache invalidation (fixed in PR 678). This is the real cutover window for v2.14. Main goals: avoid cold-cache storms, validate rollback path, and coordinate comms with CS/ops.

Schedule (UTC):
- 08:30 - pre-cutover sync (zoom + #release) quick go/no-go
- 09:00 - start staggered deploy to canary pool (10% traffic)
- 09:20 - monitor canary (latency, error rate, mem)
- 09:40 - promote to 50% (if metrics healthy)
- 10:00 - full rollout + post-cutover checks

Pre-cutover checklist (do before 08:30):
- [ ] Confirm on-call roster: Ellis (lead), Aisha (rollback), Jordan (monitoring), Riley (infra)
- [ ] Lock down changelog + release notes (linked artifact above)
- [ ] Verify backups and snapshot schedule (DB snapshot + config backups)
- [ ] Ensure feature flags for new routing are togglable from console
- [ ] Confirm cache priming script readiness (scripts/prime-cache.sh) and staging results
- [ ] Export list of long-running queries / jobs to pause during cutover

Canary (09:00 -> 09:20):
- Deploy canary to dedicated pool (tag: release/v2.14-canary)
- Commands: 
  - kubectl -n inference set image deployment/serving-runtime serving-runtime=registry/redwood/serving:v2.14-canary
  - ./scripts/deploy-canary.sh --pool canary --tag v2.14-canary
- Monitor dashboards:
  - latency: dash/serving-runtime/p50-p99
  - errors: dash/serving-runtime/error-rate
  - throughput: dash/serving-runtime/tps
  - cache hitrate: dash/cache/hitrate
- Acceptance: p99 latency <= baseline + 25ms, error rate < 0.5% for 15m
- If fail: abort promotion, rollback canary via kubectl rollout undo, notify #release, open JIRA ENG-2345-FAIL

Promotion to 50% (09:40):
- Gradually increase traffic-weight in router (route-control CLI) to 50% over 5m
- Watch for spikes in CPU/GPU utilization and KV cache miss rate
- Run smoke tests: 
  - smoke/smoke-chat.sh 
  - smoke/embeddings-quick.sh
- Check logs for exceptions: 
  - kubectl logs -n inference -l app=serving-runtime --since=10m | egrep "ERROR|panic|OOM"

Full rollout (10:00):
- Promote tag to stable and update autoscaler profiles if needed
- Post-cutover validation: run full test harness (approx 20m) and confirm metrics stable
- Announce release: #release -> Stakeholders, CS, and infra channels; include rollback instructions

Backports & cherry-picks (high priority):
- PR 678 (KV cache race fix) -> must be included in every release pool
- Backport checklist: 
  - repo: inference-runtime branch: release/2.x PR: 681-backport-v2.14
  - run unit tests: ./ci/run-tests.sh --suite=unit --fast
  - run critical e2e subset: ./ci/run-tests.sh --suite=e2e-critical

Rollback plan (if >=1% errors or p99 regression >50ms sustained 10m):
- Immediate action: flip routing back to previous tag (v2.13-stable) via route-control rollback --tag v2.13-stable
- Trigger postmortem bridge: #postmortem and create JIRA ENG-2345-rollback with logs attached
- Revert DB/config changes staged in migration plan (see linked confluence)

Monitoring checklist (continuous):
- Watch p50/p90/p99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU util, cache hitrate, DB latencies
- Pager thresholds: error rate > 1% (pager), p99 > baseline + 100ms (pager)
- Dashboards to keep open: latency, errors, cache, infra-alloc, autoscaler metrics

Comms (short):
- Pre-cutover (08:45): post short note to #release with canary start time and expected window
- Canary green (09:25): quick update -> stakeholders: "canary healthy, promoting to 50%"
- Full rollout (10:05): longer note with links to dashboards and rollback steps
- Post-cutover (10:30): summary + any known issues + follow-ups

Post-cutover follow-ups (owners):
- [ ] Performance regression triage (Jordan) - due EOD
- [ ] Update runbook with lessons learned (Ellis) - due +3 days
- [ ] Confirm billing/usage for dedicated pools (Finance cc) - Riley

Open questions / TODOs (quick):
- Is the autoscaler profile change required for v2.14? (ask infra)
- Do we need an extra 30-minute cool-down before full rollout to avoid cache stampede?
- Should we priming list include top-50 prefixes only or top-200? (cost tradeoff)

Quick commands to keep handy:
- Rollback routing: route-control rollback --tag v2.13-stable
- Canary deploy: ./scripts/deploy-canary.sh --pool canary --tag v2.14-canary
- Prime cache: ./scripts/prime-cache.sh --targets top-50 --parallel 5
- Tail logs (errors): kubectl logs -n inference -l app=serving-runtime -f | egrep "ERROR|panic"

Notes to self: keep comms crisp, default to rollback on unclear failures, prioritize user-facing error visibility over internal perf blips. If anything goes sideways, call Aisha first (she owns rollback sequences).
